core_obligations: Prove, for a cartesian square of algebraic spaces with g and f Tor independent: (1) if E in D(O_X) has tor amplitude in [a, b] as a complex of f^{-1}O_Y-modules, then L(g')^*E has tor amplitude in [a, b] as a complex of f'^{-1}O_{Y'}-modules; (2) if G is an O_X-module flat over Y, then L(g')^*G = (g')^*G
proof_roadmap: Compute at stalks: the derived pullback of E at a geometric point of X' is E_x tensor^L over O_{X,x} the local ring of X'; tor independence identifies this with E_x tensor^L over O_{Y,y} the local ring of Y'.
Part (1) follows from the pull-tor-amplitude lemma since the tensor product with the local ring of Y' has tor amplitude contained in [a, b].
Part (2): flatness of G is equivalent to G[0] having tor amplitude in [0, 0]; applying part (1) gives L(g')^*G = (g')^*G.
difficulty_reason: H2: a stalk-level computation that routes the tor amplitude statement through two standard lemmas.
